statement: The owner's two signature inputs (RT + RB + a right-stick flick, RT + a right-stick flick) cannot be pressed: with RT held the right stick is switched off in the input layer, and the only signature input is RT + B.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: an input read on an existing reader, a director entry for two signatures, tests and a golden window
risk: RT is also the charge hold, so a flick on RT can collide with charging; a claw-grip check and the stray-beam count would show it early.
orb_question: Should RT + B stop being a signature once your two stick inputs exist? Recommendation: yes, retire RT + B so no beam can start from a face button.

statement: Couch 2v2 with four pads cannot be played: the input hub holds two human slots per PC and every pad routine loops over two.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: the two-slot join rule took one built-and-tested pass (docs/controls/local-two-player.md:3, join_test 53 checks); four slots repeats it with per-slot settings and remap files
risk: Per-player settings and remap files are written for two players (presets and presets_p2); a four-pad join test would show breakage early.

statement: Each fighter's move table has no outcome for 18 of 101 cells and 65 cells reach the same entry as another cell; the LB, LT and RT rows of the face buttons mostly repeat the no-stance row.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the count is from main's data, and the played build turns on four more cell switches that were not re-counted
risk: The table's size is itself undecided (A has no mash or hold design), so work could aim at cells nobody wants; a signed cell list first avoids it.

statement: A right-stick beam that is refused at release waits and fires by itself up to 90 ticks later, and did so in the owner's last match 33 ticks after the stick was let go, during a brawl started with a face button.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one wait rule and its test
risk: Dropping the waiting beam too early makes an intended beam feel swallowed; the press ledger's refused count would show it.

statement: The pad as the owner plays it is not the default in data: eleven input switches are off on main and on in both played builds only through the private page's switch table.
cost_basis: comparable: the earlier flip of twelve input switches needed a patch across 15 files and a regenerated golden (docs/controls/pending/landing/README.md:13-16, uncommitted); no token figure recorded
risk: Any build not made through the switch table plays a different pad from the one the owner approved; reading each build's packed timing.json shows it.

statement: A pad unplugged mid-match does not pause or show a notice: player two's fighter is handed to the computer and player one is moved to the keyboard while the match runs on.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one host rule, one notice, one test row
risk: A pause on unplug must not fire for a pad nobody is playing; the join test's third-pad row would show it.
orb_question: When a pad drops out mid-match, should the game pause with a plain notice instead of handing the fighter to the computer? Recommendation: yes, pause in every local mode.

statement: The flight speed the owner preferred (3500) exists only as a slider on the private browser page; the data's default is 5000, the energy model that reads it is off on main, and the LAN setup sends no flight speed.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one data value, re-reads of the checks keyed to it, and a golden window if the model is turned on in data
risk: Speeds by level multiply the base (flatOut x growth^level), and the trail's start speed and dash closing times are keyed to absolute speeds; power_check and a look at the trail would show a mismatch.
orb_question: Should 3500 become the default flight speed for every mode, with the slider dropped until a real setting exists? Recommendation: yes.

statement: The latest count of unanswered presses is from an older build: 225 of 760 presses not honoured (30 percent), 97 of them with no word or buzz, and no count exists for the build the owner last played.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one ledger run on the two saved play files (S), then the director-side drops that still say nothing
risk: The ledger's counting rule changed twice (7 and 8 Nov), so counts across builds are not like for like; fixing the rule before the next count avoids a false trend.

statement: No moveset coverage probe exists: the nearest tool presses each input alone for 90 ticks and its saved result is from a tree of 1 November.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: extend the case table to held button by face button by press kind and the stick, per fighter, with a duplicate check
risk: A probe that reads main's data would pass or fail a pad nobody plays; it must read the build's packed data.

statement: The Steam Deck's built-in controls have never been tried: no run on a Deck or through Steam's pad layer is on record, and the project's own Deck page marks it untested.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: a ten-minute pad checklist for a tester with a Deck, and a reading of its result
risk: Outside Steam's own store the Deck may present its controls differently to a game added by hand; the first tester's checklist shows it.

statement: The press-to-picture latency record is not current: it measures the browser build with keyboard presses on 22 and 23 October, before the right-stick scheme, and nothing measures a pad, the desktop build or a Deck.
cost_basis: comparable: the October record's re-runs reused one bench (docs/perf/tools/latency-bench.mjs); no token figure recorded
risk: The bench drives key events; a pad or stick press needs a scripted pad, which the bench does not have.

statement: The quick LT tap still carries the fighter further than the ruled step when far from the rival (9.9 body heights against a bound of 6.5), and was not measured against a moving rival.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one lever and a re-run of the existing tap matrix
risk: The step and the flight speed pull on each other; settle the flight speed first, then re-read the matrix.

statement: With RT + B kept as the interim signature, B fires a signature for as long as RT is held and the fighter is not charging, not only in the first 12 ticks the rule's own comment states.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; it disappears if RT + B is retired (F-CONTROLS-01)

statement: None of the 46 input test scripts runs in CI; the only saved run is the Executive Producer's local gate, where 45 ran and passed (the 46th file, mash_probe, is a probe).
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one CI job over existing scripts
risk: Thirteen older tests pin the switches off to pass; a CI job must keep that or they fail by design.

statement: Control and comfort settings are saved and reloaded in code, but no test restarts the game on Windows or Linux to prove it, and the saved-options load is skipped for scripted runs.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one two-launch test per platform
risk: The save folder is shared by every copy of the project on a PC, so one build's saved remap can meet another build's layouts.

statement: Keyboard play is bound for every action on the solo layout but is unproven on the played build, and two players on one keyboard get a weaker strike (one key plus the movement direction).
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: run the coverage probe (F-CONTROLS-09) through the keyboard layout
risk: Beam aim from four arrow keys is coarser than a stick; whether it can aim between the four directions is not evidenced.
orb_question: For Alpha, is 'keyboard works, a pad is recommended' enough, with full keyboard equality left for Beta? Recommendation: yes, since the outside testers play on a Deck.

statement: Leftovers stay live in the input layer: bindings and hints for three power specials that are switched off, a keyboard class nothing calls, and touch layouts and phone vibration while mobile is parked.
risk: Whether the Specials hint row is ever drawn was not traced; a still of the hints screen settles it.

statement: The controls folder's index is out of date and 51 parked paths sit uncommitted, some already on main, so the folder cannot be trusted to say what is landed.
risk: A stale park re-applied by mistake; checking main before any apply avoids it.

statement: The base of the owner's pad scheme is the default in data on main and in both played builds: the Arena preset, the right-stick strikes, the beam aim, the quick read and the signature on RT only.
Two pads on one PC each drive their own fighter: the start menu gives the first pad to player one and the second to player two, and the join rule's tests passed in the saved local gate.

Remapping per player, a left-handed mirror of every pad preset and a left-handed keyboard preset exist in code and data, save to a player file that is read at start-up, and passed their tests in the saved local gate.
The host reads pads by Godot's standard button and axis positions, so the engine's own pad mappings decide what a Deck sends; back buttons and trackpads are not read and are not needed.
A written latency budget exists (first visible reaction within 3 ticks, 50 ms before the display) and guard and dash were measured reacting on the next tick in the browser build.
A refused press can be told: the pad's refusal knock is on in data, the hub lists refusals with a reason code, and the director's refused cue is on in the played build.
A tool that lists every beam a player started, with the buttons held just before, exists and found the stray beam in the owner's saved match.
